anchor_definition: The anchor is the first target-specific value-construction function on the dynamic behavior chain: the earliest function, after routing and input preparation, whose own body constructs the target observable value rather than merely collecting inputs, dispatching control, packaging the result, or emitting it to the sink or fetch call.

primary_anchor.source_export: private helper reached through exported u(config)
primary_anchor.answer_basis: Agent-visible corpus only: the canonical anchor answer is captured_span plus answer_function as declared in the captured bundle slice. source_function is a private maintainer mapping into src/.
primary_anchor.why: Constructs the target exposure_digest by folding the exposure triple cells (user key, flag key, send-exposure bit, envelope version, plane, speed) through the runtime-selected reducer variant, combining the fold result with the exposure state frame and formatting the 16-char base36 digest with the ex_ prefix that is placed into the flag.exposure console object and the /api/exposure fetch body.

acceptable_hit_conditions: Canonical match is primary_anchor.captured_span in the captured bundle (hash/offset/complete function body). Agents only see captures, so the standard answer identifier is primary_anchor.answer_function, not source_function.

A returned function name is scored against answer_function in the captured corpus. source_function is a private maintainer label and is not something an agent can know unless the bundle still exposes that exact identifier.
Agent explanation distinguishes the anchor from routing, input preparation, wrapper, sink, transport write, core utility and off-chain decoy functions.
A snippet answer is accepted only when it maps uniquely to one complete enclosing function in the captured corpus.

scoring_policy.source_level_answer: not_applicable_for_default_agent_corpus; grade by captured_span and answer_function only
scoring_policy.span_overlap_policy: score by the unique role_oracle row whose captured_span fully contains the submitted span, or whose captured_span is fully contained by a uniquely submitted enclosing function span

do_not_promote: The final console sink and fetch transport emit an already constructed exposure_digest value.
The exported factory only wraps the private exposure-payload anchor and should not outrank the anchor itself.
User/flag collection, version reading and tuple building are generic preparation, not the target value constructor.
The flagCellMark/exposureAuditCandidate chain is an inactive decoy and is not called by the exposure_digest encode path.
The shadow_exposure debug emitter writes a ctx-styled fake frame and is off the target chain.
Non-target flag.assign/flag.audit console objects can carry exposure_digest-like values but are not the requested observable action.
debug_hints_private: Canonical anchor answer id: primary_anchor.answer_function at primary_anchor.captured_span in the captured bundle.
primary_anchor.source_function is only for maintainer mapping back to src/ and may differ after obfuscation.
The target field name (exposure_digest) and the /api/exposure URL are assembled at the sink from character-code arrays.
The delegated click action key is 2:58:4 (lane 2, kind 4, weight 58); the async queue fires in order mutation -> frame -> then -> micro -> timer; the local event plane channel is z0:exposure-plane.
Source paths are private evaluator mapping aids, not the default answer space.
captured_span coordinates are regenerated by scripts/gen_oracle_spans.mjs after npm run build.

scoring_examples.matched_reason: Returned span maps uniquely to primary_anchor.captured_span; answer_function matches the buildExposurePayload declaration in that captured bundle slice.
Returned span maps to a target-specific helper below the anchor, such as encodeExposureDigest, exposureStateFrame, buildExposureCells or runFold.
Returned span maps to a generic utility directly used by the digest construction path, or the base36 folder and envelope serializer reused by non-target emitters.
Returned span maps to a path-critical routing/materialization/wrapper function or the final output wrapper.
Returned span maps to a generic DOM, tuple, version or field-name helper used in upstream preparation.
Returned span maps to an off-chain decoy or cannot be uniquely mapped to a captured function.
